docs.title: FinPulse AI
docs.text:
Self-hosted invoice and expense tracking with an optional AI receipt scanner.

Try it first

Open the interactive demo and click Continue as Guest. It is a static preview of the real interface; the full app runs locally through Docker.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Stores invoices with line items, due dates and statuses.
  • Records expenses from a form or from a scanned receipt.
  • Extracts merchant, date, tax, totals and items from pasted text offline, or from images/PDFs with Gemini.
  • Renders cashflow and category charts as inline SVG — no CDN, no tracking.
  • Seeds 14 invoices and 18 expenses on first boot so the dashboard is never empty.

docs.title: Three-minute start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/priyanshkk/finpulse-ai.git
cd finpulse-ai
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d

Visit http://localhost:8000. Press Refresh demo data in the sidebar to re-seed.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
DATABASE_URL defaults to a SQLite file under ./data, which is gitignored and mounted into the container. Add GEMINI_API_KEY only if you want image/PDF OCR. Without it, text receipts are parsed locally and nothing is sent to an external service.

Continue with Usage or the API reference.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Interactive OpenAPI docs are served at /docs and the schema at /openapi.json when the app is running.

Method Path Purpose GET /api/health Readiness probe returning status and version GET /api/dashboard KPIs, monthly series, category slices, recent records GET /api/invoices Newest 100 invoices POST /api/invoices Create an invoice with line items DELETE /api/invoices/{id} Delete one invoice GET /api/expenses Newest 100 expenses POST /api/expenses Create an expense DELETE /api/expenses/{id} Delete one expense POST /api/scan Extract fields from text, JSON, or an uploaded file POST /api/seed Insert demo data once

docs.title: Scan pasted text
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/scan \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"filename":"receipt.txt","text":"Blue Tokai
12/04/2026
Coffee beans 2 x 450.00
GST 18% 162.00
TOTAL 1,062.00"}'

The response contains merchant, purchase_date, total, tax, currency, items, confidence, engine and note. Validation errors return standard FastAPI 422 payloads; oversized uploads return 413; missing records return 404.

All amounts use Decimal in Python and numeric strings in JSON, so rounding never depends on binary floats.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
FinPulse AI is a single-process web app. The browser talks to FastAPI, which owns the business rules; Gemini is an optional step inside the receipt service; SQLite (or PostgreSQL) is the only source of truth.

flowchart LR
    A[Frontend\nJinja2 + CSS + inline SVG] --> B[Backend\nFastAPI routers + services]
    B --> C{AI needed?\nimage / PDF}
    C -->|yes, key set| D[Gemini API\ngenerateContent JSON]
    C -->|no or key missing| E[Offline regex parser]
    D --> F[Validated ScanResult]
    E --> F
    F --> B
    B --> G[(Database\nSQLAlchemy 2\nSQLite / PostgreSQL)]
    G --> B
    B --> A

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
routers/web.py renders four server-side pages, while routers/api.py exposes the same operations as JSON. Both call services/ledger.py, which validates input through Pydantic schemas, derives line-item and invoice totals, and commits through a short-lived SQLAlchemy session from db.py.

Receipt uploads go through services/receipts.py. With GEMINI_API_KEY set, the service sends the extracted text to Gemini's generateContent endpoint and validates the returned JSON into a ScanResult. Any network error, malformed reply or missing key falls back to the deterministic regex parser, so the app is never blocked by an outage. Users review the extracted fields before scan/save creates an expense.

services/analytics.py aggregates invoices and expenses into monthly buckets and category slices, and services/charts.py turns those into SVG strings. Charts are rendered on the server, so there is no JavaScript chart library or CDN request.

services/seed.py inserts 14 invoices and 18 expenses with random.Random(42) when SEED_ON_START=1. The seed is idempotent and marks its rows with source="seed", so clear_seed() can remove them without touching your data. Configuration comes only from environment variables in .env.

docs.title: Contributing to FinPulse AI
docs.text: This guide gets you from clone to pull request in a few minutes.

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
Python 3.11+ is required. Use a virtual environment:

git clone https://github.com/priyanshkk/finpulse-ai.git
cd finpulse-ai
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cp .env.example .env             # Windows: copy .env.example .env
python -m uvicorn finpulse_ai.main:app --reload --port 8000

Set PYTHONPATH=src on Windows if the package is not installed. For tests, use an in-memory database and disable seeding: DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///:memory: SEED_ON_START=0 python -m pytest.

docs.title: Before you open a PR
docs.text:
Run the same checks CI runs:

python -m pytest
python -m ruff check .
python -m ruff format --check .
python -m mypy src/finpulse_ai

Add a test for every change. Keep functions typed, never commit .env or API keys.

docs.title: Branches and commits
docs.text: Create a branch from main with a conventional prefix: feat/login, fix/currency-rounding, docs/docker-guide, test/ocr-fallback. Write commit messages in Conventional Commits form: feat: add PDF export for monthly invoices, fix: resolve currency rounding issue in dashboard, docs: add docker setup instructions.

docs.title: Pull request steps
docs.text:
1. Rebase on the latest main and confirm the four checks above pass.
  2. Describe what changed and how you verified it; attach a screenshot for UI work.
  3. Link the related issue and request one reviewer. Keep PRs focused — one idea per PR.

By contributing you agree that your work is licensed under MIT.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The overview page shows four KPIs — total invoiced, total expenses, net cashflow and outstanding amount — followed by a six-month cashflow chart and a spend-by-category chart. Every number comes from the database on each request.

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text: Invoices are numbered INV-YEAR-NNNN automatically. Create them through the JSON API with POST /api/invoices. subtotal is the sum of quantity × unit_price, total adds tax, and due_at is never earlier than the issue date plus one day. Status is one of paid, pending or overdue.

docs.title: Scanning receipts
docs.text:
Open /scan in the browser. Paste the receipt text (a .txt file also works) and submit. The offline parser looks for a merchant on the first line, an ISO or DD/MM/YYYY date, TOTAL and GST/tax lines, and lines shaped like Coffee beans 2 x 450.00.

Review the extracted fields, then press Save as expense. Nothing is persisted until you confirm.

For image or PDF OCR, set a real key in .env:

GEMINI_API_KEY=your_real_key
GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.0-flash

The service posts to Gemini's generateContent endpoint with responseMimeType=application/json. If the key is a placeholder, missing, or the request fails, it silently falls back to the offline parser and reports the engine on screen.

docs.title: Demo data
docs.text: SEED_ON_START=1 seeds once. Run POST /api/seed or click Refresh demo data any time; the operation is idempotent. Set SEED_ON_START=0 for a clean database.

docs.title: Running from source
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
set PYTHONPATH=src             # macOS/Linux: export PYTHONPATH=src
python -m uvicorn finpulse_ai.main:app --reload
